claim: NGF sensitizes pain-receptor neurons through increased trafficking of TRPV1 channels to the plasma membrane.
source: Although it has been known for over a decade that the inflammatory mediator NGF sensitizes pain-receptor neurons through increased trafficking of TRPV1 channels to the plasma membrane, the mechanism by which this occurs remains mysterious.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, referencing what has been known for over a decade.

claim: NGF activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K).
source: NGF activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), the enzyme that generates PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3, and PI3K activity is required for sensitization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: PI3K generates PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3.
source: NGF activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), the enzyme that generates PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3, and PI3K activity is required for sensitization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PI3K enzymatic activity.

claim: PI3K activity is required for NGF-induced sensitization.
source: NGF activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), the enzyme that generates PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3, and PI3K activity is required for sensitization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The N-terminal region of TRPV1 interacts directly with PI3K.
source: One tantalizing hint came from the finding that the N-terminal region of TRPV1 interacts directly with PI3K.
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding that provides context for the current study.

claim: TRPV1 potentiates NGF-induced PI3K activity.
source: Using two-color total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy, we show that TRPV1 potentiates NGF-induced PI3K activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrated using TIRF microscopy.

claim: A soluble TRPV1 fragment corresponding to the N-terminal Ankyrin repeats domain (ARD) is sufficient to produce potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity.
source: A soluble TRPV1 fragment corresponding to the N-terminal Ankyrin repeats domain (ARD) was sufficient to produce this potentiation, indicating that allosteric regulation was involved.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experiments with the ARD fragment.

claim: Allosteric regulation is involved in TRPV1 potentiation of PI3K activity.
source: A soluble TRPV1 fragment corresponding to the N-terminal Ankyrin repeats domain (ARD) was sufficient to produce this potentiation, indicating that allosteric regulation was involved.
evidence: This is inferred from the sufficiency of a soluble fragment to produce potentiation.

claim: Other TRPV channels with conserved ARDs also potentiated NGF-induced PI3K activity.
source: Further, other TRPV channels with conserved ARDs also potentiated NGF-induced PI3K activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study extending the observation to other TRPV channels.

claim: There is reciprocal regulation of PI3K signaling by the ARD of TRPV channels.
source: Our data demonstrate a novel reciprocal regulation of PI3K signaling by the ARD of TRPV channels.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: Inflammatory hyperalgesia is hypersensitivity to thermal, chemical, and mechanical stimuli.
source: Inflammatory hyperalgesia, the hypersensitivity to thermal, chemical, and mechanical stimuli (Cesare and McNaughton, 1996), can be divided in two phases, acute and chronic (Dickenson and Sullivan, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: Inflammatory hyperalgesia can be divided into two phases: acute and chronic.
source: Inflammatory hyperalgesia, the hypersensitivity to thermal, chemical, and mechanical stimuli (Cesare and McNaughton, 1996), can be divided in two phases, acute and chronic (Dickenson and Sullivan, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Locally released inflammatory mediators include growth factors, bradykinin, prostaglandins, ATP and tissue acidification.
source: Locally released inflammatory mediators, including growth factors, bradykinin, prostaglandins, ATP and tissue acidification (Kozik et al., 1998; Lardner, 2001; Tissot et al., 1989; Burnstock, 1972), directly stimulate and sensitize nociceptive fibers of primary sensory neurons (Cesare and McNaughton, 1996; Bevan and Yeats, 1991; Trebino et al., 2003; Hamilton et al., 1999; Mcmahon et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Inflammatory mediators directly stimulate and sensitize nociceptive fibers of primary sensory neurons.
source: Locally released inflammatory mediators, including growth factors, bradykinin, prostaglandins, ATP and tissue acidification (Kozik et al., 1998; Lardner, 2001; Tissot et al., 1989; Burnstock, 1972), directly stimulate and sensitize nociceptive fibers of primary sensory neurons (Cesare and McNaughton, 1996; Bevan and Yeats, 1991; Trebino et al., 2003; Hamilton et al., 1999; Mcmahon et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: TRPV1 is a non-selective cation channel.
source: TRPV1 is a non-selective cation channel that is activated by a variety of noxious stimuli including heat, extracellular protons, and chemicals including capsaicin, a spicy compound in chili pepper (Caterina et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: TRPV1 is activated by heat, extracellular protons, and capsaicin.
source: TRPV1 is a non-selective cation channel that is activated by a variety of noxious stimuli including heat, extracellular protons, and chemicals including capsaicin, a spicy compound in chili pepper (Caterina et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: TRPV1 is expressed in sensory nociceptive neurons with cell bodies located in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and trigeminal ganglia.
source: TRPV1 is expressed in sensory nociceptive neurons, which are characterized by cell bodies located in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and trigeminal ganglia (Caterina et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Sensory afferents from TRPV1-expressing neurons project to skin and internal organs, and synapse onto interneurons in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord.
source: Sensory afferents from these neurons project to skin and internal organs, and synapse onto interneurons in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord (Willis, 1978).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: TRPV1 activation leads to sodium and calcium influx, which results in action potential generation in the sensory neuron and pain sensation.
source: TRPV1 activation leads to sodium and calcium influx, which results in action potential generation in the sensory neuron and, ultimately, pain sensation (Caterina et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The TRPV1 knock-out mouse showed decreased thermal pain responses and impaired inflammation-induced thermal and chemical hyperalgesia.
source: The importance of TRPV1 in inflammatory hyperalgesia was demonstrated by findings that the TRPV1 knock-out mouse showed decreased thermal pain responses and impaired inflammation-induced thermal and chemical hyperalgesia (Caterina et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: TRPV1 currents are enhanced during inflammation which leads to increased pain and lowered pain thresholds.
source: TRPV1 currents are enhanced during inflammation which leads to increased pain and lowered pain thresholds (Davis et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2005; Shu and Mendell, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: TRPV1 is modulated by G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs).
source: TRPV1 is modulated by G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), but the mechanisms by which these receptors modulate and sensitize TRPV1 are controversial (Suh and Oh, 2005; Shu and Mendell, 1999; Cesare and McNaughton, 1996).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: NGF acts directly on peptidergic C-fiber nociceptors.
source: NGF acts directly on peptidergic C-fiber nociceptors (Donnerer et al., 1992), which express RTK receptors for NGF: Tropomyosin-receptor-kinase A (TrkA) (Mcmahon et al., 1995) and neurotrophin receptor p75NTR (Lee et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Peptidergic C-fiber nociceptors express TrkA and p75NTR receptors for NGF.
source: NGF acts directly on peptidergic C-fiber nociceptors (Donnerer et al., 1992), which express RTK receptors for NGF: Tropomyosin-receptor-kinase A (TrkA) (Mcmahon et al., 1995) and neurotrophin receptor p75NTR (Lee et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: NGF binding to TrkA/p75NTR induces receptor auto-phosphorylation and activation of downstream signaling pathways including PLC, MAPK, and Type IA PI3K.
source: NGF binding to TrkA/p75NTR induces receptor auto-phosphorylation and activation of downstream signaling pathways including phospholipase C (PLC), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and Type IA phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) (Vetter et al., 1991; Raffioni and Bradshaw, 1992; Dikic et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The acute phase of NGF-induced sensitization requires activation of PI3K, which increases trafficking of TRPV1 channels to the PM.
source: We and others have previously shown that the acute phase of NGF-induced sensitization requires activation of PI3K, which increases trafficking of TRPV1 channels to the PM (Stein et al., 2006; Bonnington and McNaughton, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as previous findings with citations.

claim: In chronic pain, NGF produces changes in the protein expression of ion channels such as TRPV1 and NaV1.8.
source: In chronic pain, NGF also produces changes in the protein expression of ion channels such as TRPV1 and NaV1.8 (Ji et al., 2002; Thakor et al., 2009; Keh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Type 1A PI3K phosphorylates PI4P and PIP2 into PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3, respectively.
source: Type 1A PI3K is a lipid kinase, which phosphorylates the signaling lipids Phosphatidylinositol (4) phosphate (PI4P) and Phosphatidylinositol (4,5) bisphosphate (PIP2) into Phosphatidylinositol (3,4) bis phosphate (PI(3,4)P2)and Phosphatidylinositol (3,4,5) trisphosphate (PIP3), respectively (Auger et al., 1989).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3 are signaling lipids with well-established roles in membrane trafficking and other downstream signaling.
source: PI(3,4)P2 and PIP3 are signaling lipids as well, and their role in membrane trafficking and other downstream signaling is well-established (Insall and Weiner, 2001; Hawkins and Stephens, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: PI3K is an obligatory heterodimer that includes the catalytic p110 subunit and regulatory p85 subunit.
source: PI3K is an obligatory heterodimer that includes the catalytic p110 subunit (with α, β, and γ isoforms) and regulatory p85 subunit (with α and β isoforms) (Hiles et al., 1992; Vanhaesebroeck et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The p85 subunit contains two Src homology 2 (SH2) domains.
source: The p85 subunit contains two Src homology 2 (SH2) domains (Escobedo et al., 1991), which recognize the phospho-tyrosine motif Y-X-X-M of many activated RTKs and adaptor proteins (Songyang et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The SH2 domains of p85 recognize the phospho-tyrosine motif Y-X-X-M of many activated RTKs and adaptor proteins.
source: The p85 subunit contains two Src homology 2 (SH2) domains (Escobedo et al., 1991), which recognize the phospho-tyrosine motif Y-X-X-M of many activated RTKs and adaptor proteins (Songyang et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In the resting state, p85 inhibits the enzymatic activity of p110 via one of its SH2 domains.
source: In the resting state, p85 inhibits the enzymatic activity of p110 via one of its SH2 domains (Miled et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Autoinhibition of p110 by p85 is relieved when p85 binds to a phospho-tyrosine motif.
source: This autoinhibition is relieved when p85 binds to a phospho-tyrosine motif (Miled et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: NGF-induced PI3K activity leads to an increase in the number of TRPV1 channels at the PM.
source: NGF-induced PI3K activity leads to an increase in the number of TRPV1 channels at the PM (Bonnington and McNaughton, 2003; Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: TRPV1 and p85 interact directly.
source: We have previously shown that TRPV1 and p85 interact directly (Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding with a citation.

claim: The TRPV1/p85 interaction was localized to the N-terminal region of TRPV1 and a region including two SH2 domains of p85.
source: We localized the TRPV1/p85 interaction to the N-terminal region of TRPV1 and a region including two SH2 domains of p85 (Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding with a citation.

claim: The functional interaction site for p85 is localized to the region of TRPV1 N-terminus containing several conserved Ankyrin repeats (ARD).
source: Here, we further localized the functional interaction site for p85 to the region of TRPV1 N-terminus containing several conserved Ankyrin repeats (Ankyrin repeat domain (ARD)).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study.

claim: The ARD is structurally conserved among TRPV channels.
source: Because the ARD is structurally conserved among TRPV channels, we tested whether other TRPV channels could also potentiate NGF-induced PI3K activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge that motivated the experiments.

claim: TRPV2 and TRPV4 both potentiated NGF-induced PI3K activity.
source: We found that TRPV2 and TRPV4 both potentiated NGF-induced PI3K activity and trafficked to the PM in response to NGF.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: TRPV2 and TRPV4 trafficked to the PM in response to NGF.
source: We found that TRPV2 and TRPV4 both potentiated NGF-induced PI3K activity and trafficked to the PM in response to NGF.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Upon addition of NGF, TRPV1 levels at the PM increased.
source: Consistent with previous findings (Stein et al., 2006), upon addition of NGF, TRPV1 levels at the PM increased, with time point two depicting the cell footprint intensity at steady state.
evidence: This is demonstrated by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: NGF treatment produced a significant increase in Akt-PH levels compared to vehicle (Mean ± SEM: 1.54 ± 0.08, n = 122 compared to 1.01 ± 0.01, n = 32, Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−12).
source: NGF induced a significant increase in Akt-PH levels compared to vehicle (Mean ± SEM: 1.54 ± 0.08, n = 122 compared to 1.01 ± 0.01, n = 32, Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−12, Figure 1C, top panel, orange and black symbols respectively, see also Figure 1—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy data with statistical analysis.

claim: NGF treatment produced a significant increase in TRPV1 levels compared to vehicle (Mean ± SEM: 1.15 ± 0.02, n = 94 compared to 0.99 ± 0.01, n = 20, Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−6).
source: and a significant increase in TRPV1 levels compared to vehicle (Mean ± SEM: 1.15 ± 0.02, n = 94 compared to 0.99 ± 0.01, n = 20, Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−6; Figure 1C, bottom panel, orange and black symbols respectively, see also Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy data with statistical analysis.

claim: The NGF-induced increases in both PM-associated Akt-PH and TRPV1 were prevented by the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin (20 nM).
source: Consistent with a PI3K-dependent mechanism, the NGF-induced increases in both PM-associated Akt-PH and TRPV1 were prevented by the PI3K inhibitor wortmannin (20 nM) (Figure 1C and D, magenta, n = 60, Mean ±SEM for Akt-PH – 0.88 ± 0.01 and for TRPV1 – 0.95 ± 0.01; Wilcoxon rank test p value for Akt-PH – 10−13 and for TRPV1 – 10−10).
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy data with pharmacological inhibition.

claim: Btk-PH completely abrogated NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 to the PM.
source: We found that Btk-PH completely abrogated NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 to the PM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments shown in supplementary data.

claim: Akt-PH was fully compatible with NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1.
source: In contrast, Akt-PH was fully compatible with NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments validating the use of Akt-PH probe.

claim: NGF-induced Akt phosphorylation was preserved in cells expressing the Akt-PH probe.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 2 shows that NGF-induced Akt phosphorylation was preserved in cells expressing the Akt-PH probe.
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in supplementary data.

claim: The ratio of total fluorescence intensity measured after and before NGF application (FNGF) of 1.54 translates into about a 10-fold increase in PM-associated fluorescence (Rm).
source: Under our experimental conditions, we estimate that the ratio of the total fluorescence intensity measured after and before NGF application, FNGF, of 1.54 translates into about a 10-fold increase in PM-associated fluorescence, Rm (Figure 1—figure supplement 4; see Materials and methods), although this should be considered just a rough estimate.
evidence: This is an estimate based on modeling of TIRF illumination depth.

claim: NGF-induced PI3K activity was greater in TRPV1-expressing cells than in cells without TRPV1.
source: Comparing the NGF-induced increase in Akt-PH in control cells that did not express TRPV1 to that in cells expressing TRPV1, we made an unexpected observation: TRPV1 appeared to potentiate NGF-induced PI3K activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study comparing TRPV1-expressing and control cells.

claim: The peak normalized Akt-PH intensity value was 1.08 ± 0.03 (n = 75) in cells without TRPV1 and 1.54 ± 0.08 (n = 122) in cells expressing TRPV1, which was statistically significant (Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−12).
source: This increase was statistically significant, with the peak normalized Akt-PH intensity value of 1.08 ± 0.03 (n = 75) in cells without TRPV1 and 1.54 ± 0.08 (n = 122) in cells expressing TRPV1 (Figure 2B, Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−12, see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding with statistical analysis comparing TRPV1-expressing and control cells.

claim: Expression of TRPV1 did not alter the expression level of the p85α subunit of PI3K.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, expression of TRPV1 did not alter the expression level of the p85α subunit of PI3K.
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in supplementary data.

claim: Average relative p85α expression levels were similar between non-TRPV1 expressing cells and cells expressing TRPV1 (n = 5, Student's t-test p value was 0.95).
source: Average relative p85α expression levels were similar between non-TRPV1 expressing cells and cells expressing TRPV1 (n = 5, Student's t-test p value was 0.95).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from western blot analysis with statistical testing.

claim: NGF induced PI3K activity that was greater in TRPV1-ARD expressing cells than in control cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2A (gray trace), NGF induced PI3K activity that was greater in TRPV1-ARD expressing cells than in control cells (blue trace).
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy comparing ARD-expressing and control cells.

claim: The increase in peak Akt-PH normalized intensity in TRPV1-ARD expressing cells was statistically significant compared to control cells, with a mean of 1.32 (±0.02, n = 80; Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−5).
source: The increase in peak Akt-PH normalized intensity was statistically significant compared to control cells, with a mean of 1.32 (±0.02, n = 80; Figure 2B; Wilcoxon rank test p = 10−5, see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding with statistical analysis.

claim: The potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity by the ARD fragment was nearly as great as observed with full-length TRPV1 (Wilcoxon rank test p = 0.08).
source: Nevertheless, the potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity by the ARD fragment was nearly as great as observed with full-length TRPV1 (Wilcoxon rank test p = 0.08).
evidence: This is a comparative finding with statistical analysis.

claim: The ability of a soluble TRPV1 fragment to reconstitute potentiation suggests that the mechanism of potentiation is at least partly allosteric.
source: In addition, the ability of a soluble TRPV1 fragment to reconstitute potentiation suggests that the mechanism of potentiation is at least partly allosteric, involving more than just a tethering of PI3K at the membrane by TRPV1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the sufficiency of the soluble ARD fragment.

claim: TRPV1-expressing cells showed increased phosphorylation at both T308 and S473 compared to control cells for almost all trials with all three NGF concentrations and both time points.
source: We observed increased phosphorylation at both T308 and S473 in TRPV1-expressing cells compared to control cells for almost all trials with all three NGF concentrations and both time points (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The enhanced NGF-induced Akt phosphorylation was statistically significant for both T308 and S473 sites for all conditions pooled together (paired Student's t-test for T308 p = 0.02 and S473 p = 0.008).
source: The enhanced NGF-induced Akt phosphorylation was statistically significant for both T308 and S473 sites for all conditions pooled together (Figure 3D,E; paired Student's t-test for T308 p = 0.02 and S473 p = 0.008).
evidence: This is a primary finding with statistical analysis from western blot data.

claim: TRPV1 potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity is sufficient to enhance PI(3,4)P2 and/or PIP3 levels to increase Akt phosphorylation.
source: Thus, TRPV1 potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity is sufficient to enhance PI(3,4)P2 and/or PIP3 levels to increase Akt phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Akt phosphorylation data.

claim: The extent of Akt phosphorylation in unstimulated cells was indistinguishable in control vs. TRPV1-expressing cells at both S308 and T473 sites.
source: Finally, Figure 3 shows that the extent of Akt phosphorylation in unstimulated cells was indistinguishable in control vs. TRPV1-expressing cells at both S308 (IntensitypAkt/pan Akt: 0.075 ± 0.004 for control and 0.076 ± 0.004 for TRPV1, Mean ± SEM, n = 3, paired Student's t-test p = 0.95) and T473 sites (IntensitypAkt/pan Akt: 0.3 ± 0.24 for control and 0.23 ± 0.14 for TRPV1, Mean ± SEM, n = 3, paired Student's t-test p = 0.44)
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis with statistical testing.

claim: TRPV1 did not perturb the levels of PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 at rest.
source: indicating that TRPV1 did not perturb the levels of PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 at rest.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar basal Akt phosphorylation levels.

claim: NGF-induced phosphorylation of Akt was not observed in cells in which TrkA/p75NTR were not expressed.
source: Importantly, we examined whether NGF-induced phosphorylation at both T308 and S473 required expression of TrkA/p75NTR. NGF-induced phosphorylation of Akt was not observed in cells in which TrkA/p75NTR were not expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot analysis shown in supplementary data.

claim: NGF-induced PI3K activity is greater, and PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 production is greater, in TRPV1-expressing cells than in those that do not express TRPV1.
source: Together with the data using Akt-PH in TIRF microscopy experiments, these data indicate that NGF-induced PI3K activity is greater, and PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 production is greater, in TRPV1-expressing cells than in those that do not express TRPV1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including TIRF and western blot data.

claim: The ARD of TRPV1 is highly conserved among other members of the TRPV family of ion channels.
source: The ARD of TRPV1 is highly conserved among other members of the TRPV family of ion channels (Gaudet, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: TRPV2 and TRPV4 were both trafficked to the PM in response to NGF compared to vehicle (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05).
source: Using TRPV2 and TRPV4 fused to fluorescent proteins, we found that they were both trafficked to the PM in response to NGF compared to vehicle (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05 see Table 1, Figure 4C,D, see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1 for representative images).
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy with statistical analysis.

claim: The NGF-induced increase in Akt-PH was significantly greater in TRPV2- and TRPV4-expressing cells compared to control cells (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05).
source: In addition, we found that the NGF-induced increase in Akt-PH was significantly greater in TRPV2- and TRPV4-expressing cells compared to control cells (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05 see Table 2, Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated by TIRF microscopy with statistical analysis.

claim: The effects of TRPV2 and TRPV4 on PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 levels were significantly smaller than those elicited by TRPV1 (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05).
source: The effects of TRPV2 and TRPV4 on PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 levels were significantly smaller than those elicited by TRPV1 (Holm-Bonferroni post-hoc adjusted Wilcoxon rank test p < 0.05 see Table 2).
evidence: This is a comparative finding with statistical analysis.

claim: Potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity and traffic to the PM in response to NGF are conserved among TRPV1, TRPV2, and TRPV4.
source: We conclude that potentiation of NGF-induced PI3K activity and traffic to the PM in response to NGF are conserved among TRPV1, TRPV2, and TRPV4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on multiple TRPV channels.

claim: Increased trafficking of TRPV1 to the cell surface is essential for sensitization to noxious stimuli produced by NGF and other inflammatory mediators.
source: Increased trafficking of TRPV1 to the cell surface is essential for sensitization to noxious stimuli produced by NGF and other inflammatory mediators (Morenilla-Palao et al., 2004; Ferrandiz-Huertas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Without TRPV1 potentiation of PI3K, NGF signaling would not produce sufficient PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 to promote channel trafficking during inflammation.
source: We speculate that, without TRPV1 potentiation of PI3K, NGF signaling would not produce sufficient PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 to promote channel trafficking during inflammation.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: TRPV2 is co-expressed in muscle cells with the insulin like growth factor receptor (IGFR) and is important in muscle loss during muscular dystrophy.
source: For example, TRPV2 is co-expressed in muscle cells with the insulin like growth factor receptor (IGFR) and is known to be important in muscle loss during muscular dystrophy (Iwata et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The mechanism of muscle loss in muscular dystrophy is believed to involve IGFR activation leading to increased trafficking of TRPV2 to the sarcolemma, Ca2+ overload/cytotoxicity, and cell death.
source: The mechanism is believed to involve IGFR activation leading to increased trafficking of TRPV2 to the sarcolemma, Ca2+ overload/cytotoxicity, and cell death (Iwata et al., 2003; Perálvarez-Marín et al., 2013; Katanosaka et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: TRPV channels are co-expressed with RTK/PI3K in nerve (TRPV1/NGF), muscle (TRPV2/IGF) and lung (TRPV4/TGFβ1).
source: The co-expression of TRPV channels with RTK/PI3K in other tissues, including nerve (TRPV1/NGF) (Tanaka et al., 2016), muscle (TRPV2/IGF) (Katanosaka et al., 2014) and lung (TRPV4/TGFβ1) (Rahaman et al., 2014) raises the question of whether reciprocal regulation among TRPV channels and PI3K plays a role in RTK signaling in cell development, motility, and/or pathology.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Reciprocal regulation among TRPV channels and PI3K may play a role in RTK signaling in cell development, motility, and/or pathology.
source: The co-expression of TRPV channels with RTK/PI3K in other tissues, including nerve (TRPV1/NGF) (Tanaka et al., 2016), muscle (TRPV2/IGF) (Katanosaka et al., 2014) and lung (TRPV4/TGFβ1) (Rahaman et al., 2014) raises the question of whether reciprocal regulation among TRPV channels and PI3K plays a role in RTK signaling in cell development, motility, and/or pathology.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a question/speculation by the authors.

claim: TIRF microscopy isolates approximately 100 nm of the cell proximal to the coverslip.
source: TIRF microscopy isolates ~ 100 nm of the cell proximal to the coverslip (Ambrose, 1961; Axelrod, 1981), capturing the PM-proximal fluorescent signals.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the TIRF technique with citations.

claim: A change in TRPV1 fluorescence reflects a change in the number of TRPV1 channels at the PM.
source: A change in TRPV1 fluorescence reflects a change in the number of TRPV1 channels at the PM.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the TIRF microscopy measurements.

claim: A change in PH domain probe fluorescence reflects a change in PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 concentration at the PM.
source: A change in PH domain probe fluorescence reflects a change in PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 concentration at the PM, thus serving as an indirect measure of PI3K activity.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the PH probe measurements.

claim: Akt is phosphorylated in a PI(3,4)P2/PIP3-dependent manner at two sites, T308 and S473, by PDK1 and mTORC2, respectively.
source: Akt is phosphorylated in a PI(3,4)P2/PIP3-dependent manner at two sites, T308 and S473, by PDK1 (Alessi et al., 1997; Stokoe et al., 1997; Frech et al., 1997) and mTORC2, respectively (Sarbassov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Phosphorylation of Akt at T308 and S473 leads to full activation of Akt.
source: Phosphorylation of Akt at these two sites leads to full activation of Akt, regulating a variety of cellular processes, including the inflammatory response to NGF (Xu et al., 2007; Sun et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: With a typical TIRF setup, approximately 90% of the signal comes from the cytosol.
source: Nevertheless, with a typical TIRF setup such as that used for this study (see Materials and methods) ~90% of the signal comes from the cytosol (Figure 1—figure supplement 4, also see Materials and methods), assuming the incident light was at the critical angle and that the membrane bilayer and associated protein layer extends up to ~10 nm from the coverslip.
evidence: This is calculated based on modeling of TIRF illumination depth.

claim: The contamination of the TIRF signal with fluorescence from the cytosol leads to an underestimation of the change in PM-associated fluorescence from Akt-PH and TRPV1.
source: The contamination of the TIRF signal with fluorescence from the cytosol leads to an underestimation of the change in PM-associated fluorescence from Akt-PH and TRPV1.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of cytosolic contamination in TIRF measurements.

claim: The dynamics of NGF-induced PI(3,4)P2/PIP3-generation in the absence of TRPV1 were different in that PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 levels were sustained.
source: Interestingly, the dynamics of NGF-induced PI(3,4)P2/PIP3-generation in the absence of TRPV1 were also different in that PI(3,4)P2/PIP3 levels were sustained.
evidence: This is an observation from the time course data comparing TRPV1-expressing and control cells.

claim: The kinetics of potentiation by TRPV1-ARD were somewhat slower compared to TRPV1, so that Akt-PH reached steady-state levels somewhat later during NGF treatment.
source: The kinetics of this potentiation were somewhat slower with TRPV1-ARD compared to TRPV1 (Figure 2A, orange trace), so that Akt-PH reached steady-state levels somewhat later during NGF treatment.
evidence: This is an observation from the time course data comparing TRPV1 and TRPV1-ARD.

claim: The direct interaction between TRPV1 and PI3K mediates the signaling for potentiation of PI3K activity.
source: In addition, whereas the present work does not rule out that the potentiation of PI3K we describe requires an effector that mediates signaling between the TRPV1 ARD and PI3K, we favor a simpler model in which the previously described direct interaction between TRPV1 and PI3K mediates the signaling.
evidence: This is stated as the authors' favored model/interpretation.

claim: The distribution of NGF-induced TRPV1 sensitization in F-11 cells is skewed toward larger values, which is characteristic of NGF-induced TRPV1 sensitization reported previously in DRG neurons.
source: The distributions were not normal, but skewed toward larger values. This distribution shape is characteristic of NGF-induced TRPV1 sensitization reported previously in DRG neurons (Stein et al., 2006; Bonnington and McNaughton, 2003), indicating that our cell expression model behaves similarly to isolated DRG neurons.
evidence: This is an observation about the data distribution with comparison to previous findings.
